.gitlab-ci.yml:2: info artifacts-no-expiry
  The default artifacts have no expire_in; jobs "lint" and "audit" use them.
  why: Artifacts without expire_in are kept as long as the instance default
       allows: 30 days on GitLab.com, possibly forever on a self-managed
       instance. Most job artifacts are only needed by the next stages of the
       same pipeline.
  fix:
    default:
      artifacts:
        expire_in: 1 week

.gitlab-ci.yml:2: warning floating-image
  The default image "node:latest" uses the latest tag; jobs "lint" and "audit"
  use it.
  why: A floating image changes under the pipeline without any commit: the same
       commit can pass today and fail tomorrow, and nothing can be rebuilt as it
       was. `docker buildx imagetools inspect node:<version>` prints the digest.
  fix:
    default:
      image: node:<version>@sha256:<digest>

.gitlab-ci.yml:8: info no-cache
  Job "lint" installs dependencies with npm but has no cache.
  why: Without a cache, every run downloads the same packages again: time on
       each pipeline, and a failure whenever the registry is slow or down. A
       cache keyed on the lockfile is reused until the dependencies change.
  fix:
    lint:
      variables:
        npm_config_cache: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.npm
      cache:
        - key:
            files: [package-lock.json]
          paths: [.npm/]

.gitlab-ci.yml:8: warning no-rules
  Job "lint" has no rules, only or except, so GitLab's defaults decide where it
  runs.
  why: By default a job runs on every branch and every tag. With workflow:
       rules, or with the project setting that skips branch pipelines for merge
       requests, it runs in every pipeline instead, merge requests included.
       Either way it rarely runs only where it is needed.
  fix:
    lint:
      rules:
        - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

.gitlab-ci.yml:8: error redundant-job
  Job "lint" runs 2 times for the same commit: on the default branch and on the
  tag.
  why: With merged results pipelines and no direct pushes to the default branch,
       the merge request pipeline already tests the exact commit that lands on
       the default branch, and a tag only names that commit. Running the job
       again there cannot find anything new; it only costs runner time and
       delays the release.
  fix:
    lint:
      rules:
        - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

.gitlab-ci.yml:8: info stages-without-needs
  4 jobs declare no needs:, so each waits for every job of the earlier stages:
  "lint", "unit", "audit" and "e2e".
  why: Without needs:, a job starts only when every job of the earlier stages
       has finished, even those it does not use: the pipeline lasts as long as
       the slowest job of each stage, added up. With needs:, a job starts as
       soon as the jobs it lists are done. The suggestion takes needs: from
       dependencies: where the job declares them.
  fix:
    lint:
      needs: [<jobs it uses>]
    unit:
      needs: [<jobs it uses>]
    audit:
      needs: [<jobs it uses>]
    e2e:
      needs: [<jobs it uses>]

.gitlab-ci.yml:12: info artifacts-no-expiry
  Job "unit" keeps its artifacts with no expire_in.
  why: Artifacts without expire_in are kept as long as the instance default
       allows: 30 days on GitLab.com, possibly forever on a self-managed
       instance. Most job artifacts are only needed by the next stages of the
       same pipeline.
  fix:
    unit:
      artifacts:
        expire_in: 1 week

.gitlab-ci.yml:12: info floating-image
  Job "unit" runs in image "golang:1.26", which is pinned by tag but not by
  digest.
  why: A tag can be pushed again with other content. A digest pins the exact
       image, so a rebuild uses the same bytes. `docker buildx imagetools
       inspect golang:1.26` prints the digest.
  fix:
    unit:
      image: golang:1.26@sha256:<digest>

.gitlab-ci.yml:12: info missing-interruptible
  Job "unit" runs on merge requests but does not set interruptible.
  why: When a new commit is pushed to a merge request, GitLab can cancel the
       pipeline of the previous commit, but a job that has started is cancelled
       only if it is interruptible. This one keeps running for a commit nobody
       will merge. Setting interruptible: true under default: covers every job
       at once.
  fix:
    unit:
      interruptible: true

.gitlab-ci.yml:23: warning unresolved-reference
  !reference [.missing] could not be found; what it stands for is treated as
  unknown.
  why: pipewise cannot tell what this part stands for, so the jobs that depend
       on it are reported as "maybe".

.gitlab-ci.yml:26: warning e2e-everywhere
  Job "e2e" is an end-to-end suite and runs 2 times for the same commit: on the
  merge request and on the default branch.
  why: End-to-end suites are usually the slowest jobs of a pipeline, and on the
       same commit they give the same answer on every event: each extra run adds
       their full duration to the pipeline. Run the suite once, on the merge
       request, where it can still stop the merge; if it is too slow for merge
       requests, run it on the default branch only.
  fix:
    e2e:
      rules:
        - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

.gitlab-ci.yml:26: error redundant-job
  Job "e2e" runs 2 times for the same commit: on the merge request and on the
  default branch.
  why: With merged results pipelines and no direct pushes to the default branch,
       the merge request pipeline already tests the exact commit that lands on
       the default branch, and a tag only names that commit. Running the job
       again there cannot find anything new; it only costs runner time and
       delays the release.
  fix:
    e2e:
      rules:
        - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"

.gitlab-ci.yml:37: warning version-baked-at-build
  Build job "build" reads CI_COMMIT_TAG in its script, so the tag pipeline
  builds an artifact that no merge request tested.
  why: The merge request pipeline tested an artifact built without the tag; the
       tag pipeline builds a new one and ships it untested. Build once with the
       commit SHA, then on the tag only retag or promote that artifact, and
       inject the version at deploy time.
  fix:
    build:
      # build with the commit SHA, never the tag
      script:
        - docker build -t $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHA .
    retag:
      stage: deploy
      script:
        - docker buildx imagetools create -t $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_TAG $CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHA
      rules:
        - if: $CI_COMMIT_TAG

.gitlab-ci.yml: 13 findings: 2 errors, 5 warnings, 6 info.
